sentences.text: Eopinacosaurus is noted for its pronounced squamosal horns, a feature reflected in its specific name meaning “devilish” head.
A large articulated skeleton was uncovered in 1996 by a Belgian-Chinese expedition in China’s Bayan Mandahu Formation.
The specimen, catalogued as IMM 96BM3/1, was originally described as Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 1999.
In 2026 Paul Penkalski reassigned the material to the newly erected genus Eopinacosaurus.
Eopinacosaurus belongs to the dinosaur order Ornithischia, family Ankylosauridae, and is placed within the ankylosaurid subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
The genus is monotypic, containing only the species Eopinacosaurus mephistocephalus.
Its fossils come from the Late Cretaceous Campanian deposits of the Bayan Mandahu Formation in China and the Djadokhta Formation in Mongolia.
Eopinacosaurus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
Gregory S. Paul proposed in 2010 that Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus might be a junior synonym of Pinacosaurus grangeri, implying they represent the same species.
Subsequent phylogenetic analyses have placed Eopinacosaurus in varying positions within the ankylosaurine clade relative to the type species of Pinacosaurus, reflecting ongoing uncertainty.
